correctness.rationale: For every negative edge, a uniformly positive receptive weight bounds the selection hazard between constants times the exponentially decaying power of its own count. Conditional geometric upper/lower tails are summable; Borel–Cantelli gives logarithmic waiting-time growth and its inverse logarithmic count law. Bounded martingale strong law establishes positive-edge selection frequencies and exponential deficit rates; countable restarting/coupling extends it to eventual stabilization. The proof does not mistake finite numerical checks for an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The nearest primary source (Thompsky et al., arXiv:2605.20418v1, Theorems 2–3) proves limit weights and graph stabilization but not the a.s. inverse-time exponent or exact logarithmic contact counts. McNulty–Raban (arXiv:2607.20818v1, Sections 2.1–2.3 and Appendix B) proves positive limiting frequencies for the all-discount sampler, requiring every exponent strictly positive, which does not cover any persistently receptive edge whose weight approaches one. The exact proposed mixed-sign limits follow from different conditional geometric waiting-time estimates; relevant searches uncovered no identical covered result. Unrecognized broader urn/sampling theorem remains a risk.

value.rationale: The primary social-dynamics paper proves only binary weight limits; knowing a discordant tie fades gives no information about its calendar-time residual interaction burden. The exact nonzero logarithmic encounter law, universal inverse-time weight exponent despite heterogeneous forgetting parameters, and contrasting exponential receptive recovery quantify how persistent receptive ties structurally alter observation and mixing frequencies. A three-agent path realizes the phenomenon without special status-switch assumptions. The asymptotic cutoff is motivated by the model's communication overhead, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
